essential_question: Which of the things I do now will still be possible next year?
learning_objectives: Perform, adapt, or describe auditing current activities against post-graduation reality safely at an intensity, range, and pace the learner sets.
Explain the movement, tactical, or training principle behind auditing current activities against post-graduation reality and why it works.
Self-assess auditing current activities against post-graduation reality against stated criteria and name the next adjustment, without comparing to any other person.
success_criteria: The learner completes or fully describes the auditing current activities against post-graduation reality task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule before any work on auditing current activities against post-graduation reality.

Teach the cues, principle, or tactic behind auditing current activities against post-graduation reality. Demonstrate or describe it, name the critical features, and show at least one adapted version alongside the standard version — not after it.

Practise auditing current activities against post-graduation reality with feedback on cues and decisions only. Feedback addresses the movement or the choice, never the learner's body, size, or appearance. Fade prompting as control improves.
Learner applies auditing current activities against post-graduation reality in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, what they noticed, and what they would adjust.

Cool down, then in one concise response explain the key idea behind auditing current activities against post-graduation reality and name one adjustment for next session. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner applies auditing current activities against post-graduation reality in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
formative_check: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind auditing current activities against post-graduation reality and name one adjustment for the next session.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of auditing current activities against post-graduation reality — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind auditing current activities against post-graduation reality before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of auditing current activities against post-graduation reality, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of auditing current activities against post-graduation reality; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.

Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking auditing current activities against post-graduation reality mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Apply auditing current activities against post-graduation reality under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
The audit may be written, tabled, or spoken. A learner whose next year is uncertain builds the plan against two or three scenarios instead of one.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
No household income, address, or family financial detail is entered into course records; cost planning uses general figures the learner supplies at whatever precision they choose.
inclusive_adaptation: The audit may be written, tabled, or spoken. A learner whose next year is uncertain builds the plan against two or three scenarios instead of one.

guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian discusses realistic post-graduation constraints with the learner; nothing financial is recorded by the course.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting auditing current activities against post-graduation reality.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of auditing current activities against post-graduation reality in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

essential_question: What would I like to be genuinely good at, and what will that cost me?
learning_objectives: Perform, adapt, or describe setting a challenging but achievable personal goal safely at an intensity, range, and pace the learner sets.
Explain the movement, tactical, or training principle behind setting a challenging but achievable personal goal and why it works.
Self-assess setting a challenging but achievable personal goal against stated criteria and name the next adjustment, without comparing to any other person.
success_criteria: The learner completes or fully describes the setting a challenging but achievable personal goal task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.
materials: equipment appropriate to the chosen challenge

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule before any work on setting a challenging but achievable personal goal.

Teach the cues, principle, or tactic behind setting a challenging but achievable personal goal. Demonstrate or describe it, name the critical features, and show at least one adapted version alongside the standard version — not after it.

Practise setting a challenging but achievable personal goal with feedback on cues and decisions only. Feedback addresses the movement or the choice, never the learner's body, size, or appearance. Fade prompting as control improves.
Learner applies setting a challenging but achievable personal goal in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, what they noticed, and what they would adjust.
Cool down, then in one concise response explain the key idea behind setting a challenging but achievable personal goal and name one adjustment for next session. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner applies setting a challenging but achievable personal goal in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
formative_check: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind setting a challenging but achievable personal goal and name one adjustment for the next session.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of setting a challenging but achievable personal goal — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind setting a challenging but achievable personal goal before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of setting a challenging but achievable personal goal, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.
Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of setting a challenging but achievable personal goal; the alternate route is full credit and is not logged as a refusal.
Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking setting a challenging but achievable personal goal mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Apply setting a challenging but achievable personal goal under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
The challenge is defined entirely by the learner relative to their own current capability; any goal that is meaningful and safe for that learner qualifies.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
The challenge is never a body-composition, weight, or appearance goal, is never compared to another person’s result, and is never required to be witnessed, filmed, or published.
inclusive_adaptation: The challenge is defined entirely by the learner relative to their own current capability; any goal that is meaningful and safe for that learner qualifies.

guardian_safety.environment: Guardian approves the location and conditions.
guardian_safety.movement_hazards: The challenge is the highest-demand task in the course. Guardian reviews and approves the goal, the preparation, and the attempt conditions before the attempt.
guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian sets supervision for the attempt and may require it to be supervised or declined.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting setting a challenging but achievable personal goal.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of setting a challenging but achievable personal goal in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

essential_question: What does taking care of myself look like when no one is telling me to?
learning_objectives: Sustain illness, injury, and graded return without a coach built as a learner-managed protocol for a full training-block scenario, executed when guardian-approved or fully modelled, including a realistic stop decision and the required adult-escalation boundary, holding the critical features when conditions stop being ideal. Full transfer credit requires the complete block protocol, warning cue, stop decision, recovery boundary, and adult-escalation step. Guardian-approved execution, a table, or a full written or described model earns equal credit when all of that safety reasoning is present.
Explain what changed about illness, injury, and graded return without a coach under that demand, and which cue or principle held and which broke down first.
Judge the learner's own illness, injury, and graded return without a coach against the criteria a second time and account for the difference from the first pass.
success_criteria: The learner holds illness, injury, and graded return without a coach built as a learner-managed protocol for a full training-block scenario, executed when guardian-approved or fully modelled, including a realistic stop decision and the required adult-escalation boundary, in whatever version their body and setting allow. Full transfer credit requires the complete block protocol, warning cue, stop decision, recovery boundary, and adult-escalation step. Guardian-approved execution, a table, or a full written or described model earns equal credit when all of that safety reasoning is present.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Run the space, surface, footwear, and equipment check, then a learner-led warm-up. Restate the stop rule, and name the added demand explicitly before starting: illness, injury, and graded return without a coach built as a learner-managed protocol for a full training-block scenario, executed when guardian-approved or fully modelled, including a realistic stop decision and the required adult-escalation boundary.

Have the learner restate the critical features of illness, injury, and graded return without a coach from the earlier pass before any demonstration. Then introduce the transfer condition and ask which feature they expect to lose first, and why. Keep the adapted version available on equal terms.

Work illness, injury, and graded return without a coach built as a learner-managed protocol for a full training-block scenario, executed when guardian-approved or fully modelled, including a realistic stop decision and the required adult-escalation boundary. Feedback stays on the cue or the decision, never on the learner's body, size, or appearance. Reduce the demand rather than the standard if control breaks down, and say that is the intended response, not a failure.

Learner works illness, injury, and graded return without a coach independently under the condition at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.

Cool down, then in one concise response account for the difference between the two occasions of illness, injury, and graded return without a coach and name the adjustment that carries forward. No recording or photograph is taken.

student_activity: Learner works illness, injury, and graded return without a coach built as a learner-managed protocol for a full training-block scenario, executed when guardian-approved or fully modelled, including a realistic stop decision and the required adult-escalation boundary at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one. Full transfer credit requires the complete block protocol, warning cue, stop decision, recovery boundary, and adult-escalation step. Guardian-approved execution, a table, or a full written or described model earns equal credit when all of that safety reasoning is present.
formative_check: In one concise response, say which feature of illness, injury, and graded return without a coach degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score safe participation, skill cues, tactical reasoning, self-management, and revision. Accept any version of the task the learner’s body and setting allow as full credit when it supplies the stated transfer evidence. Never score body size, weight, body composition, appearance, speed alone, or comparison with another person. Full transfer credit requires the complete block protocol, warning cue, stop decision, recovery boundary, and adult-escalation step. Guardian-approved execution, a table, or a full written or described model earns equal credit when all of that safety reasoning is present.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the simplest version of illness, injury, and graded return without a coach — slower, smaller range, closer target, or seated — then rebuild.
Ask the learner to explain the cue or tactic behind illness, injury, and graded return without a coach before adding intensity or complexity.
Confirm the specific cue that worked, offer one varied application of illness, injury, and graded return without a coach, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable movement pattern neutrally, contrast it with the critical features, and schedule varied practice.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: pain, dizziness, breathlessness, or head impact
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Stop immediately, tell an adult, and do not resume in this session. This is never recorded as a failed attempt.

Offer the adapted, seated, solo, or described version of illness, injury, and graded return without a coach; the alternate route is full credit when it supplies the stated transfer evidence and is not logged as a refusal. Full transfer credit requires the complete block protocol, warning cue, stop decision, recovery boundary, and adult-escalation step. Guardian-approved execution, a table, or a full written or described model earns equal credit when all of that safety reasoning is present.

adaptive_tutor_routes.signal: transfer condition is too much today
adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Drop back to the first-pass version of illness, injury, and graded return without a coach for this session and re-attempt the added demand on a later occasion. Reducing the demand is the correct response and is scored as full participation, but it does not itself satisfy the transfer evidence requirement.
Require accurate independent performance or description plus explanation on a later occasion or in a different setting before marking illness, injury, and graded return without a coach mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one session. Use safe participation, skill cues, tactical decisions, self-management, personal progress against the learner’s own stated task, and self-assessment — without body-size scoring; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions separated by time or setting.
extension: Design the next progression of illness, injury, and graded return without a coach yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
The protocol may be written, tabled, or described; a learner managing an ongoing condition builds it with guardian input around constraints they already have.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about bodies, ability, and effort.
Allow a pause, rest, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Check space, footwear, surface, weather, and equipment before movement.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing difficulty, head impact, or unsafe conditions and tell an adult.
Score skill, strategy, self-management, consistency, and reflection — never body size, weight, weight change, body composition, appearance, or comparison with another person.
Do not require weight, BMI, body-fat, body measurement, fitness-test norms, percentile ranks, calorie counts, or diet goals at any point.
Do not require a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as evidence; described, written, and demonstrated-to-one-adult evidence is the intended route.
Do not require performance in front of an audience, a group, or spectators.
No body measurement, wearable export, sleep log, or health data is requested or recorded. The protocol is written in the learner’s own descriptive language.
inclusive_adaptation: The protocol may be written, tabled, or described; a learner managing an ongoing condition builds it with guardian input around constraints they already have.

guardian_safety.supervision_note: Guardian reviews the protocol and confirms the household escalation path to a clinician. The course does not diagnose.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, described demonstration, or short clip supporting illness, injury, and graded return without a coach.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, cue lists, alt text, a transcript, or an adult demonstration. No lesson requires media, and no learner media is ever produced.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose body data, fitness scores, photographs, video, recordings, or comparisons with other learners. For safety-critical units, record only the guardian confirmation that was required.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice where illness, injury, and graded return without a coach shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.
